message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the last common ancestor of the two orders that contain them—Carnivora (the order that includes cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and Perissodactyla (the odd‑toed ungulates that include horses, rhinos, and zebras).  

That ancestor is the most recent common ancestor of all placental mammals (the eutherian ancestor), which lived roughly 100–120 million years ago during the early Cretaceous. In other words, lions and zebras share a very distant common ancestor that is the root of the placental mammal tree.
